messages:
eric: Quick follow-up after the RFC review — we're still seeing gaps in cost attribution when enrichment rewrites spans and billing_key gets dropped. I'm proposing a small 'cost-stitcher' shim to capture pre-enrich mappings and serve quick lookups for reconciliation. Thoughts?

lina: Can you show a compact failure example?

eric: Sure. Minimal: arrival envelope with envelope_id E42 and billing_key tenant-123; enrichment rewrites spans/trace ids and emits without envelope_id, so downstream can't join on envelope.
```
// pre-enrich
envelope: { envelope_id: E42, billing_key: tenant-123 }
// post-enrich
trace: { trace_id: T99, spans: [...], billing_key: null }
```

sam: How is this different from our late-billing lookup?

eric: Late lookup assumes the join key survives. In merge/normalize paths the key is sometimes lost. Stitcher would proactively record tiny (key -> billing_key) entries at pre-enrich time so reconciliation can match on candidate identifiers (envelope-hash, tenant-hmac, span-fingerprint).

priya: Cardinality is my main worry — millions of envelopes/sec. What's storage shape and TTL?

eric: Mitigations: default TTL = 24h (configurable up to 7d), in-memory K/V (redis) with per-tenant caps + LRU, compact key form (tenant_hmac 8B + envelope_hash 12B) and small billing_key id values. Optional sampling for low-value tenants.

maria: Consider compacted kafka + local rocksdb sidecar as a cheaper option vs redis. Tradeoffs: cheaper durable storage, but higher read tail and complexity. Hybrid model possible: hot tenants to redis, cold to compacted topic.

lina: Compliance note: do not persist PII. Store only keyed HMACs or KMS-encrypted blobs; rotate keys per standard. Include auditor-visible proofs.

obs-bot: infra-bot: created ticket INF-7550 "stitcher: storage options evaluation" assigned @maria, @priya

sam: Metrics + alerts to add: stitcher.mappings.count (gauge), stitcher.hits (counter), stitcher.misses (counter), stitcher.evictions (counter), stitcher.redis_p50/95 (histogram), stitcher.backfill_queue_length (gauge). Alert if eviction_rate > 0.1% sustained or redis_p95 > 50ms.

priya: SLOs: billing reconciliation should call stitcher with a small budget (lookup_timeout_ms = 50). On miss/timeout mark event as pending and push to async backfill. User-facing path must not block. Define backfill window (suggest 6h for billing completeness).

eric: Implementation sketch: 1) pre-enrich emits compact record to topic `stitcher.snapshots` with {tenant_hmac, envelope_hash, billing_key_id} 2) stitcher consumes and writes to configured storage (redis|rocksdb|hybrid) 3) billing service queries stitcher on lookup miss with 50ms budget; on miss emit `billing.pending_stitch` for async recheck.

maria: I'll run a cost model for redis vs compacted topic + rocksdb and post numbers (RAM/cost at 1M qps, TTL 24h, sampling). Also estimate 99th percentile extra read QPS on billing path.

lina: Who owns what? Proposal: eng-platform owns service code and alerts; eng-infra owns provisioned redis clusters/backups and runbooks (including KMS rotation). Add runbook entries for eviction storms and emergency key rotation.

eric: Action items: I will draft RFC addendum covering data model, metrics, SLOs, and storage tradeoffs. Maria and Priya will produce cost/ops estimates. Lina will coordinate security/KMS language. I'll open infra-prototypes PR after RFC.

priya: +1 for prototype if per-tenant caps, TTL, and sampling are enforced. Need per-tenant quotas to prevent noisy neighbors.

eric: Thanks all — will post RFC link here when ready.
